label: Self-released
description: Hazel City's quiet debut, nine plainspoken songs of home-recorded acoustic guitar and layered vocal harmonies. It plays like a diary of a Rust Belt hometown, unhurried and intimate rather than showy.
lineage: A Gary, Indiana bedroom-folk project that grew out of the same Bandcamp DIY networks as Chicago's indie-folk scene, laying groundwork for the fuller-band goblynmarkytt.

label: Self-released
description: A nine-song set built around memorable, unfussy melodies and a rotating cast of guest vocalists, giving these hushed folk songs a communal, porch-session feel rather than a solo-singer-songwriter one.
lineage: Continues the plainspoken small-town folk of Old Friend with a wider circle of collaborators, part of the 2020s wave of Bandcamp-first indie-folk acts Josh Terry has tracked at No Expectations.

label: No Quarter
description: Recorded in a friend's upstate New York barn, this is spare, unhurried folk built from a repeating image of a bird hitting a window; Horn's guitarist trades quiet call-and-response lines with her plainspoken vocal across ten dreamlike songs.
lineage: Grew out of Horn's Austin songwriting circle and a period studying poetry; No Quarter also houses Joan Shelley, placing Horn in the same lineage of hushed, literary indie folk.

label: Self-released
description: Horn's self-titled follow-up is minimalist to the point of near-silence in places, sparse guitar figures under scalpel-precise, evocative lyric fragments; a dreamy, unhurried record that rewards close listening.
lineage: A further distillation of the hushed, literary style she developed on The Window Is The Dream.

album: It's Summer, I Love You, and I'm Surrounded by Snow
label: Self-released
description: Geneviève Beaudoin's twelve-song set swings her voice from a warble to a coo to a full scream over dark, romantic, disorienting folk arrangements; a breakup and self-reckoning record that never settles into one register for long.
lineage: Part of the Portland, Maine DIY folk scene alongside Lily Seabird's circle; Terry compared the impact of Beaudoin's voice here to first hearing Angel Olsen's Burn Your Fire.

label: Saddle Creek
description: Meg Duffy's most ambitious Hand Habits record to date, produced by Sasami Ashworth; folk-rooted songwriting opened up into lusher, more adventurous arrangements after a pandemic-forced pause, with Perfume Genius guesting on one track.
lineage: Duffy came up as an in-demand guitarist for Kevin Morby and War on Drugs before Hand Habits' own records; Fun House marks the point where the project moved from insular bedroom folk toward fuller studio arrangements.

label: Fat Possum Records
description: A love record shadowed by quiet anxiety, veering from insular early Hand Habits songwriting toward a fuzzier, 90s-indebted guitar-rock feel in the vein of Aimee Mann or Neko Case, with occasional horns and Wurlitzer.
lineage: Follows Fun House's move outward from Duffy's solo bedroom style, made as Duffy also became a full-time member of Perfume Genius's touring band.

label: Self-released
description: A Seattle bassist-singer's rich, lush-voiced solo debut of organically arranged folk songs, quiet and confident in its plainspoken storytelling.
lineage: Blackwell is primarily a bassist and guitarist in the Seattle scene; My Maze established her as a songwriter in her own right before Dream a Day.

label: Self-released
description: Ten warm, unhurried songs continuing Blackwell's plainspoken songwriting, self-released between her debut and the more widely noticed Dream a Day.
lineage: A bridge record between My Maze and Dream a Day, part of Blackwell's steady, independent Bandcamp release schedule.

label: Self-released
description: A rich, lush-voiced set of thirteen organically arranged folk songs, self-released only on Bandcamp; Blackwell's most fully realized record to date.
lineage: The culmination of Blackwell's run of independent Seattle folk records, released as her profile grew beyond her session-musician reputation.

album: I Need to Start a Garden
label: Mama Bird Recording Co.
description: Heynderickx's debut is conversational, fingerpicked folk that finds grace in the mundane, from housework to horticulture, sung in a voice that can turn from a murmur to a full-throated cry within a verse.
lineage: Emerged from Portland's DIY folk circuit; the record's patient, plainspoken observation set a template picked up by later Mama Bird and Fat Possum-adjacent songwriters like Lily Seabird.

label: Mama Bird Recording Co.
description: Ten verdant, conversational songs continuing the plainspoken observation of her debut, finding quiet grace in ordinary domestic and natural detail across a patient, guitar-centered record.
lineage: A six-years-later follow-up to I Need to Start a Garden, made after Heynderickx spent the interim touring and collaborating, including on the Max García Conover duo record.

label: Fat Possum Records
description: A duo record rooted in Woody Guthrie and radical folk history, nuanced protest songs traded between two plainspoken, patient singer-guitarists.
lineage: Connects Heynderickx's Portland folk lineage to Maine songwriter Max García Conover's own Woody Guthrie-indebted catalog.

label: Transgressive / Liberation / Polyvinyl
description: Jacklin's debut pairs a plainspoken alto with spare, twang-tinged arrangements, coming-of-age songs about leaving small-town New South Wales that sit closer to country-folk than to polished pop.
lineage: Grew from Melbourne's singer-songwriter scene; set up the more countryish overlap with Core sound that would surface fully on Pre Pleasure.
borderline_note: Debut leans closer to plain singer-songwriter pop than later records; kept in C5 per field-guide mapping.

label: Transgressive / Liberation / Polyvinyl
description: A breakup record about bodily autonomy and the end of a long relationship, delivered in Jacklin's plain, unadorned voice over spare full-band arrangements that lean acoustic more than electric.
lineage: Widely cited alongside Maple Glider and Stella Donnelly as part of a wave of Australian songwriters mining plainspoken, folk-rooted heartbreak writing.

label: Transgressive / Liberation / Polyvinyl
description: Jacklin's most overtly twang-inflected record, with clean electric guitar and horns wrapped around wry, closely observed songs about love, faith and self-image.
lineage: The clearest overlap between Jacklin's pop-folk songwriting and Core's twangy indie-folk sound, cited by Terry alongside Maple Glider's I Get Into Trouble as a touchstone.
borderline_note: Pop/indie artist's country-adjacent turn; kept in C5 (rather than Context) because the twang texture is explicit here, per brief guidance.

note: Released 25 September 2026 (day of research); confirmed via Wikipedia and Bandcamp (label 4AD) but no track titles could be confirmed from a scraped page in time.

album: Now Would Be A Good Time
label: Jagjaguwar
description: Three former high-school friends trade dazzling three-part harmonies over acoustic-led arrangements, wry and darkly funny songs about breakups, dissociation and modern early-twenties life.
lineage: Signed to Jagjaguwar (Bon Iver, Angel Olsen, Sharon Van Etten), the trio toured with Julia Jacklin and sit close to her and Stella Donnelly in the current Australian indie-folk wave.

label: Consonant Records
description: Cornfield's early full-band folk-rock record, plainspoken road-life songwriting delivered in her low, conversational alto.
lineage: Part of Cornfield's Montreal/Toronto folk-rock catalog that eventually led to the more widely noticed Could Have Done Anything.

label: Next Door Records
description: A drummer-turned-singer-songwriter's plainspoken record of quiet, groove-aware folk-rock, continuing her steady, road-worn songwriting.
lineage: Bridges Cornfield's earlier folk-rock records and the sharper, Tom Petty-esque songwriting of Could Have Done Anything.

label: Self-released
description: A patient, plainspoken record made during the pandemic, continuing Cornfield's steady run of low-key, drummer's-ear folk-rock songwriting.
lineage: Sits between The Shape of Your Name and the more widely reviewed Could Have Done Anything.

label: Next Door Records
description: Terry heard the lead single 'You and Me' as feeling 'like a Tom Petty song in the best way'; the LP is Cornfield's most confident and widely noticed record, warm folk-rock built for the road.
lineage: The culmination of Cornfield's steady solo run after years as a touring drummer for other bands.

note: Confirmed year 2026 and label Merge Records via Wikipedia, but no track titles could be confirmed from a scraped page in time.

label: RCA
description: Marten's teenage debut, hushed and delicately fingerpicked, a precociously assured folk record built around her breathy, unadorned voice.
lineage: Marten came up through YouTube covers and the UK singer-songwriter circuit before signing to RCA; this debut set the hushed template she has expanded over five albums.

label: RCA
description: A slightly more full-band second album, still built around Marten's hushed, breathy delivery and fingerstyle guitar.
lineage: Continues the debut's hushed folk approach before Marten's move to Fiction Records for Flora Fauna.

label: Fiction
description: A newly confident, full-band-driven record made after a period of writer's block, warmer and more rhythmically alive than her first two RCA albums.
lineage: Marks Marten's move from RCA to Fiction and a fuller, more grounded folk-pop sound.

label: Fiction
description: A warm, love-steeped record, softer and more contented in tone than Flora Fauna, still built on Marten's fingerstyle guitar and close vocal harmonies.
lineage: Continues Marten's Fiction-era run toward fuller, twangier folk arrangements ahead of Dog Eared.

label: Fiction
description: Marten's most commanding record, full-band indie folk with twangy melodies and earthy production, a marked step up in scale from her hushed early albums.
lineage: The clearest example yet of Marten's folk songwriting picking up genuine twang texture, per Terry's review.

label: Northern Spy Records
description: Krieger's early Northern Spy record: undulating, plainspoken diaristic songwriting over spare acoustic arrangements, quieter and rawer than her later, more piercing work.
lineage: The start of Krieger's run of prolific, mortality-fixated songwriting that continues through I Keep My Feet on the Fragile Plane and Art of the Unseen Infinity Machine.

album: I Keep My Feet on the Fragile Plane
label: Double Double Whammy
description: Quietly contemplative, introspective songwriting dressed with French horn, English horn and pedal steel, produced by Luke Temple; widely praised as a career high point.
lineage: Krieger's writing here drew comparisons across Terry's coverage to the strongest songwriters of her generation, ahead of the following year's Art of the Unseen Infinity Machine.
key_tracks: I Keep My Feet on the Fragile Plane

album: Art of the Unseen Infinity Machine
note: Terry dates this 2024 (Northern Spy is the likely label based on Krieger's catalog) but no scraped page confirming year/label was reached within budget.

label: Drag City
description: Pratt's second album, warbling, hazy fingerstyle folk sung in her distinctive high, cracked vibrato, associated with the freak-folk revival but closer in spirit to Vashti Bunyan than to any twang scene.
lineage: Her only album for Drag City between the self-released debut and Mexican Summer's Quiet Signs.

label: Mexican Summer / City Slang
description: A more finely produced, flute- and piano-inflected record, still built on Pratt's warbling voice and fingerstyle guitar but with a warmer, more meditative pace.
lineage: Her Mexican Summer debut, expanding her sound just ahead of Here in the Pitch.

label: Mexican Summer
description: Chilling, stripped-back folk with impressionistic lyrics and simple, immersive arrangements that Terry compared to Richard Swift's production style.
lineage: Pratt's fourth album, continuing her insular, warbling folk style within a slightly fuller sonic frame.

label: Keeled Scales
description: Kirby's early, spare full-length, quiet and melodically direct guitar-pop-folk that hinted at the more searching songwriting of Cool Dry Place.
lineage: Her first Keeled Scales release, made before she became a fixture of the Nashville/Austin indie-folk crossover.

label: Keeled Scales
description: Terry named this his 2021 album of the year: sparkling, precisely arranged indie folk-pop with an unusually sharp ear for melody, anchored by singles like 'Cubic Zirconia'.
lineage: Established Kirby as a defining voice of the 2020s indie-folk wave that runs from Nashville through Big Thief's circle.

label: ANTI-
description: A more confident, searching second album about a first queer relationship, cut with Logan Chung and Alberto Sewald and featuring a Christian Lee Hutson co-write.
lineage: Continues Kirby's move from Keeled Scales indie folk toward a bigger ANTI- platform.

label: Self-released
description: Released as Erin Rae and the Meanwhiles, a self-released early record of warm, plainspoken country-folk that predates her solo billing.
lineage: An early document of Rae's Nashville scene before Putting On Airs brought her wider attention.

label: Single Lock Records
description: Rae's breakthrough solo debut, warm and searching country-folk that examines faith, sexuality and family with unusual gentleness and directness.
lineage: Signed her to Single Lock Records and set the plainspoken, gospel-tinged style she carried into Lighten Up.

label: No Quarter
description: Shelley's No Quarter debut, patient and unadorned folk songwriting sung in a clear, plain alto over sparse guitar.
lineage: Her first record for No Quarter, the label she'd stay with through Real Warmth, part of the Louisville folk scene alongside Nathan Salsburg.

label: No Quarter
description: A quietly assured second No Quarter record, continuing Shelley's plainspoken, guitar-and-voice folk songwriting.
lineage: Bridges Electric Ursa and her self-titled 2017 breakthrough.

label: No Quarter
description: Shelley's self-titled record, produced with Jeff Tweedy's involvement, widened her audience while keeping the same plain, guitar-and-voice core.
lineage: Her most widely reviewed record before Like the River Loves the Sea, connecting her to the Wilco/Chicago folk-adjacent circle.

label: Self-released
description: A self-released, Bandcamp-only set between her label albums, in the same patient, plainspoken vein as her No Quarter records.
lineage: A stopgap independent release showing Shelley's steady, unhurried songwriting pace.

album: Like the River Loves the Sea
label: No Quarter
description: Recorded in Iceland, a warm and unhurried record continuing Shelley's plain, guitar-centered songwriting with subtly expanded arrangements.
lineage: Follows her self-titled record, keeping her within the No Quarter roster alongside Jana Horn.
key_tracks: Like the River Loves the Sea

label: No Quarter
description: A domestic, duet-filled record made with her husband Nathan Salsburg, continuing Shelley's patient, plain-voiced songwriting.
lineage: Extends the Louisville folk partnership with Salsburg that runs through her whole catalog.

label: No Quarter
description: Lush, lived-in pastoral folk with patient, transcendent songwriting, extending Shelley's decade-plus run of plain, unhurried records.
lineage: Her latest No Quarter album, keeping her among the label's core roster alongside Jana Horn and Bonny Light Horseman.

label: Self-released
description: Sofia Jensen's debut as Free Range: ten tracks of open, subdued, engaging folk begun when she was 15, evoking Elliott Smith, Lomelda and Katy Kirby in its patient, intimate delivery.
lineage: Part of the Chicago DIY folk scene alongside Hannah Frances and Jessica Risker; a quietly confident debut that led directly to Lost & Found.

label: Self-released
description: A subdued, plainspoken second album demanding close attention to Jensen's lyrics, sitting in an Elliott Smith / Adrianne Lenker lane per Terry's review.
lineage: Continues the Chicago DIY folk lineage Jensen established on Practice, now with a fuller and more confident arrangement style.

label: Ruination Record Co.
description: Seven mystifying songs pairing the knottiest folk with propulsive energy and a powerful voice, excavating grief over Frances's father's death and years of religious trauma; awarded Best New Music by Pitchfork.
lineage: Frances melds avant-folk, progressive rock and jazz; this record set up her collaboration with Daniel Rossen on Nested in Tangles.

label: Fire Talk
description: A front-to-back listen of elegant, complex forest-folk arrangements spanning progressive rock, avant-folk and jazz, with Daniel Rossen producing and arranging two tracks.
lineage: Frances's second full-length, continuing directly from Keeper of the Shepherd's exploration of familial trauma and healing.

label: Fluff and Gravy Records
description: Southwestern-raised, Portland-based songwriting with Karen Dalton-inspired vocals and psychedelic guitar, plainly indebted to Sandy Denny and country music but bent through indie songwriting.
lineage: Established Valazza in the current wave of country-folk revivalists alongside Erin Rae and Le Ren, ahead of From Newman Street.

label: Fluff and Gravy Records
description: Folk and Americana with wailing pedal steel and introspective lyrics, in the Joni Mitchell / Karen Dalton / Sandy Denny line Terry has traced through Valazza's whole catalog.
lineage: Continues Valazza's country-folk revival songwriting from Knows Nothing with a fuller pedal-steel-driven sound.
